study_type.claude: Repository mining (GitHub API mining with panel regression; new metric proposed)

research_method.claude: Repository mining via GitHub REST and GraphQL APIs; new metric Convergence Entropy (JSD-based, monthly); random-effects panel regression (Swamy-Amemiya, R plm) against SPACE-based productivity proxies
research_method.nlm: Quantitative repository mining; Convergence Entropy (JSD-based) metric proposed; longitudinal panel regression (random effects) of new bugs, new commits and issue resolution time
research_method.value: Repository mining (GitHub REST and GraphQL APIs) with a proposed information-theoretic metric (Convergence Entropy, Jensen-Shannon divergence of original vs. merged commits across forks, computed monthly); random-effects panel regression against SPACE-based project productivity proxies (new bugs, new commits, issue resolution time) with moderating control variables
research_method.note: Swamy-Amemiya estimator and R plm mentioned only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: OSS; 8 GitHub projects (4 enterprise-driven, 4 community-driven), 12,720 forks, 39,300,748 commits
context.nlm: OSS; 8 GitHub repositories (4 corporate-driven, 4 community-driven), 12,720 forks, 39,300,748 commits
context.value: OSS; 8 large GitHub projects (4 enterprise-driven: facebook/docusaurus, microsoft/playwright, alibaba/nacos, google/googletest; 4 community-driven: fastapi/fastapi, vuejs/vue, rustdesk/rustdesk, ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh); 12,720 forks and 39,300,748 commits

space_applied.note: SPACE used to select the productivity metrics (Performance: new bugs; Activity: new commits; Efficiency & Flow: issue resolution time).

remote_covid.note: Borderline: both give work mode 'not specified (distributed OSS collaboration)'; 'distributed' refers to fork-based contribution integration, not remote/hybrid work arrangements.

data_window.claude: monthly data from each project's creation to May 2025
data_window.note: Only Claude states a period (project creation to May 2025); NotebookLM gives none.

cat_productivity.note: Metrics are framed as SPACE productivity proxies but map to Quality (new bugs), Activity (new commits; NotebookLM labels it 'Productivity / Activity') and issue resolution time; neither labels issue resolution time Productivity.

cat_collaboration.note: Convergence Entropy measures integration of distributed fork contributions (crowd collaboration); computed from commit distributions, not raw commit counts.

cat_delivery.note: Issue resolution time: NotebookLM labels it 'Delivery / Efficiency & Flow'; Claude labels it only 'Efficiency & Flow (SPACE)'.

evidence.quote: We collected data on forks, commits, and all related events for each project through the GitHub REST API and GraphQL API.
To construct our linear models, we employ panel regression analysis, a robust econometric technique well-suited for our dataset, which is inherently unbalanced panel data.
In total, we collected 12,720 forks and 39,300,748 commits across these eight repositories.
Acknowledging the trend of increasing corporate involvement in open source, the sample comprises both enterprise-driven and community-driven projects.

commit activities according to the SPACE framework guidelines, spanning three dimensions: Performance, Activity, and Efficiency & Flow. These metrics are new bugs, new commits, and issue resolution time
We set up a list of bug-related keywords, i.e., defect, error, bug, issue, mistake, incorrect, fault, and flaw, and then search for these words in both the issue tags and issue titles.
Similarly, as the productivity data, we compute the number of new commits in every project-month.
A key underexplored aspect is the integration effectiveness-the degree to which distributed original commits across forks are effectively integrated back into the main repository.
